faqQ2.bellevue: How much does it cost to tile a shower in Bellevue?

faqA2.bellevue: A tiled shower in Bellevue runs $3,200 to $6,800 for a standard alcove, including demolition, a bonded waterproofing system, the pre-sloped base or pan, tile setting, a niche and grout. Curbless entries, benches, full-height stone and steam showers push above that. The waterproofing is roughly a tenth of the cost and prevents the one failure that costs tens of thousands.

faqQ3.bellevue: Do you waterproof showers before tiling?

faqA3.bellevue: Yes. Every shower we tile gets a bonded waterproofing system behind the tile, not just cement board and thinset. That means a pre-sloped base, a sheet or liquid membrane carried up the walls, sealed corners, seams and pipe penetrations, and a documented 24-hour flood test before a single tile goes on. Tile and grout are not waterproof; the membrane behind them is what keeps water out of your framing.

faqQ4.bellevue: How long does a bathroom tile job take?

faqA4.bellevue: A bathroom tile job in Bellevue takes about four to six working days: one day for demolition and dust protection, one for substrate and waterproofing plus a 24-hour flood test, one to two for setting tile, and one for grout, silicone and trim. Add 24 hours of cure time before the shower is used. Floors on their own are usually one to two days.

faqQ5.bellevue: Porcelain or ceramic tile — which is better?

faqA5.bellevue: Porcelain is the better choice for floors, showers and anything that gets wet or heavy traffic: it is denser, absorbs less than 0.5% water, and chips less. Ceramic is fine for walls and backsplashes and costs less. In Bellevue we specify porcelain for every floor and shower floor, and let ceramic or glass earn its place on walls and backsplash.

faqQ6.bellevue: Can you install a heated tile floor?

faqA6.bellevue: Yes. Electric radiant mat under tile adds about $11 to $16 per square foot installed including the thermostat, and it is the cheapest luxury in a Bellevue bathroom because it is only worth doing while the floor is already open. It goes in over an uncoupling membrane, is resistance-tested before and after setting, and runs on its own dedicated circuit.

faqQ7.bellevue: Do I need to remove the old tile first?

faqA7.bellevue: Usually yes. Old tile removal and haul-away runs about $3.50 per square foot, and it is the only way to see the subfloor, check for rot or movement, and get the new floor height right at doorways. Tiling over existing tile is possible on a sound, flat, well-bonded floor, but it raises the floor and hides problems we would rather find at demolition than after grout.
